lines.text: Two atoms can have different masses yet still be atoms of the same element. Which particle count decides whether they belong to that element?

Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. The proton number identifies the element. Adding neutrons changes the nucleon number without changing the element. For chlorine thirty five, atomic number seventeen and chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen, both proton counts are seventeen, the neutron counts are thirty five minus seventeen equals eighteen and thirty seven minus seventeen equals twenty. State both parts of the definition, same protons, different neutrons.
This definition builds on proton and nucleon number. Next, nuclide notation makes the two counts visible in one symbol.

Isotopes, atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. chlorine thirty five, atomic number seventeen and chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen both have seventeen protons, but have eighteen and twenty neutrons. Different nucleon number alone does not define isotopes, check that proton number is the same.
Why are chlorine thirty five, atomic number seventeen and chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen isotopes? Name both particle counts.

The neutral atoms chlorine thirty five, atomic number seventeen and chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen are compared. Which pair of particle counts makes them isotopes? Same protons, different neutrons Different protons, same neutrons Same protons, same neutrons Different protons, different electrons ay Both atoms have seventeen protons. Their neutron counts are eighteen and twenty, respectively. Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers.
A nuclide symbol carries enough information to count the particles in its nucleus. Reading the two numbers in the right places avoids mixing up elements and isotopes.

In x y amperes, the upper number x is the mass or nucleon number, the total number of protons and neutrons. The lower number y is the atomic or proton number, the number of protons. Therefore neutrons equals x minus y. In chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen, there are seventeen protons and twenty neutrons. The element symbol is fixed by the proton number, so isotopes of chlorine all have seventeen at the bottom.
The shared lower number shows why two atoms are the same element, different upper numbers show the neutron difference. This also supports particle counting in ions.

In x y amperes, x is nucleon, mass, number, protons plus neutrons. y is proton, atomic, number, the number of protons. Neutrons equals x minus y, chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen has thirty seven minus seventeen equals twenty neutrons. An isotope differs in neutrons, an ion differs in electrons. Charge never changes the proton or neutron count.
Explain how the top and bottom numbers of chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen tell you its proton and neutron counts.

In chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen, what do the upper and lower numbers represent? Upper, proton number, lower, neutron number Upper, nucleon number, lower, proton number Upper, neutron number, lower, electron number Upper, nucleon number, lower, neutron number B The upper thirty seven counts all nucleons, protons plus neutrons. The lower seventeen counts protons, subtracting gives thirty seven minus seventeen equals twenty neutrons.
Chlorine atoms with different neutron counts still take part in the same chemical reactions. What stays the same in the part of the atom that forms bonds?

Isotopes of the same element have the same proton number. Neutral atoms of those isotopes therefore have the same number of electrons and the same electron configuration. Chemical reactions involve electrons, especially outer electrons, so the isotopes have the same chemical properties. Their neutron counts differ, but neutrons do not take part in ordinary chemical reactions. An explanation needs both the unchanged electron configuration and its link to chemical behaviour.
The isotope definition gives the same proton number, this fixes the electron count of neutral atoms. The different neutron counts instead affect mass and density.

Neutral isotopes have the same number of electrons and the same electron configuration. Chemical reactions depend on electrons, so isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties. Different neutron counts do not change the electron configuration.
Explain why two neutral isotopes of chlorine react in the same way even though their nuclei contain different numbers of neutrons.

Neutral chlorine thirty five, atomic number seventeen and chlorine thirty seven, atomic number seventeen atoms differ in neutrons. Why do they have the same chemical properties? They have the same mass. They have the same neutron number. They have the same electron configuration. They have different proton numbers. C Both neutral atoms have seventeen protons and seventeen electrons, so their electron configurations are the same. Chemical reactions depend on electrons, while their different neutron counts change mass.
Two samples made from different isotopes can react alike yet have different masses for the same number of atoms. What measurable property of the samples might change?

Isotopes have different numbers of neutrons, and neutrons contribute to atomic mass. Their atoms therefore have different masses. A sample made from the heavier isotope has more mass for the same number of atoms, under comparable conditions this gives a different density. These are the physical properties required here. Keep the cause explicit, different neutron count to different mass to different density.
The same electrons explain matching chemical properties, the different neutrons explain different masses and densities. State each reason with its own particle.

Different neutron numbers give isotopes different atomic masses. Different mass can give samples different densities under comparable conditions. Link the physical difference to neutrons, link the chemical similarity to electrons.
Explain why thirty seven chlorine two is denser than thirty five chlorine two at the same temperature and pressure.

A sample of thirty seven chlorine two is compared with the same amount of thirty five chlorine two at the same conditions. Which property changes because of the neutron difference? Proton number Electron configuration Chemical reactions Mass and therefore density D Each chlorine thirty seven atom has two more neutrons and a greater mass. For equal amounts under the same conditions, this gives greater mass and density, while proton and electron counts are unchanged.
Which statement about the isotopes of an element is correct?

Isotopes are atoms of the same element, so the proton number is fixed, they differ only in neutrons and therefore in nucleon number. The statement about the same nucleon number but different proton numbers describes atoms of different elements.
Which particle count decides which element an atom belongs to?
Isotopes are all atoms of one element, so one of the particle counts must stay fixed and another must vary.
Test each option, would the two atoms it describes still be atoms of the same element?
Define the term isotope.
Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. Both halves are needed for full marks.
A definition has to name particles, not just say different masses.
State what stays the same and what changes, in terms of protons and neutrons.
Same number of. but different number of.
Which pair of species are isotopes of the same element?

Only the chlorine pair has the same proton number, seventeen, with different neutron numbers, eighteen and twenty. The argon and potassium pair has equal nucleon numbers but different elements, the chlorine atom and chloride ion differ only in electrons and the carbon and oxygen pair has the same number of neutrons, eight, but different protons.
Work out the protons and neutrons for each species, not just the top numbers.
For every pair, ask, same element, same proton number, and different neutron number?
Find the pair with equal bottom numbers and unequal top numbers, with no charge change.

Gallium, proton number thirty one, has two isotopes, gallium sixty nine and gallium seventy one. part a, Define the term isotope. part b, Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in a neutral atom of each isotope.

Neutrons equals nucleon number minus proton number, sixty nine minus thirty one equals thirty eight and seventy one minus thirty one equals forty. A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, thirty one.
Start from the definition, then use the two nucleon numbers.
Neutrons come from nucleon number minus proton number, a neutral atom has equal protons and electrons.
Both isotopes share the same proton and electron numbers, only the neutron numbers differ.
Atoms of argon forty, atomic number eighteen, forty nineteen kelvin and calcium forty, atomic number twenty are compared. Which statement is correct?

All three have nucleon number forty. Their proton numbers, eighteen, nineteen, twenty, differ, so they are different elements with twenty two, twenty one and twenty neutrons, so the statements about equal neutron numbers, equal electron numbers and being isotopes are wrong. Sharing a nucleon number does not make atoms isotopes.
Read the top and bottom numbers of each symbol carefully.
Isotopes need the same proton number. Do these three have it?
For each option, work out that particle count for all three atoms before deciding.

Which statements are correct when referring to the two common isotopes of chlorine? The isotopes have different masses. The isotopes have different numbers of nucleons. The isotopes have the same chemical reactions.

The two isotopes differ in neutrons, so they have different masses, one, and different nucleon numbers, two, yet the same electron configuration gives the same chemical reactions, three. Option B is wrong because statement three is also true, extra neutrons do not change the chemistry.
Take each numbered statement on its own and decide true or false.
Think about which particles change between isotopes, and which particles control chemical reactions.
Neutrons change mass and nucleon number, electrons control reactions.
In the symbol sodium twenty three, atomic number eleven, what do the two numbers show?
In the notation x y amperes the top number x is the nucleon, mass, number and the bottom number y is the proton, atomic, number. Neutrons equals twenty three minus eleven equals twelve.
One number is bigger than the other for a reason, which of them counts more particles?
The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, one number counts both, the other counts only one type.
Ask which of the two numbers could include both kinds of particle in the nucleus.
How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in the ion aluminium twenty seven three plus, atomic number thirteen?

Protons equals thirteen, bottom number. Neutrons equals twenty seven minus thirteen equals fourteen. The charge of three plus means three electrons lost from the neutral atom's thirteen, leaving ten. The wrong rows add electrons instead of removing them, sixteen, use the nucleon number as the neutron count, twenty seven, or ignore the charge, thirteen.
Read off the protons from the symbol first, then handle neutrons and electrons separately.
Neutrons, nucleon number minus proton number. Electrons, think about what a positive charge tells you.
A three plus ion has lost three electrons.

Complete the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons for each species. species, protons, neutrons, electrons. chlorine thirty five minus, atomic number seventeen. magnesium twenty four two plus, atomic number twelve. oxygen sixteen two minus, atomic number eight.
Protons equals bottom number, neutrons equals top minus bottom, electrons equals protons, charge, so a two plus ion has two fewer electrons than protons and a two minus ion has two more.
Handle the columns in order, protons, neutrons, then electrons.
Protons and neutrons ignore the charge, only the electrons depend on it.
A negative charge means extra electrons, a positive charge means fewer than the protons.
A single phosphorus thirty two nucleus can be produced when a single sulfur thirty two nucleus joins with particle X. In the process a proton is emitted. What is particle X?

The products have total nucleon number thirty two plus one equals thirty three and total proton number fifteen plus one equals sixteen. sulfur thirty two has nucleon number thirty two and proton number sixteen, so X has nucleon number one and proton number zero, a neutron. The commonly chosen B, electron, fails to balance the nucleon number, so it cannot make up the missing nucleon.
Write the reaction as a nuclear equation with top and bottom numbers.
Balance the top numbers and the bottom numbers separately, remembering the emitted proton is a product.
Subtract the reactant totals from the product totals to get the nucleon number and proton number of X, then match them to a particle.
The isotopes chlorine thirty five and chlorine thirty seven have the same chemical properties. Explain why.

Chemical properties depend on the number and arrangement of electrons, especially the outer electrons. Neutral atoms of isotopes have the same number of electrons and the same electron configuration, because they have the same number of protons.
Ask which particles take part when atoms react.
Compare the electrons of the two isotopes, not their masses.
Link the proton number of each isotope to the number of electrons in its neutral atom, then say what controls reactions.
Which property is the same for the isotopes chlorine thirty five and chlorine thirty seven?
Both have seventeen electrons in the same arrangement. Mass, neutron number and, since density depends on mass, density all differ.
Decide which of the properties depend on the nucleus and which on the electrons.
The isotopes differ in their neutrons, cross out anything that depends on neutrons.
For each option, ask whether it would change if the nucleus gained two neutrons.
Why do the isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties?
Reactions involve electrons, and isotopes have identical electron configurations. Neutrons are not involved in bonding, and isotopes differ in nucleon number and neutron number.
Which particles are transferred or shared in chemical reactions?
Consider what the isotopes share and whether that shared thing takes part in reactions.
It is not the nucleus, the shared feature is outside it.
Samples of gaseous thirty five chlorine two and thirty seven chlorine two are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

Same electron configuration means the same chemical properties, and different neutron numbers give different molecular masses and so different densities of the gas at the same temperature and pressure.
Split the question, one half about chemistry, one half about physical properties.
Chemistry depends on electrons, density depends on mass.
Check what is the same and what is different between the isotopes for each half.
A student says that carbon fourteen must be more reactive than carbon twelve because it has two extra neutrons. Explain why the student is wrong.
Neutral atoms of both isotopes have six protons and six electrons in the same configuration, and neutrons do not take part in reactions, so the chemical behaviour is the same.
Which particles decide how an atom reacts?
Compare the number and arrangement of electrons in the two isotopes.
Say what the two extra neutrons do change, then check whether they change the particles involved in reactions.

Bromine has two isotopes, bromine seventy nine and bromine eighty one. part a, Explain why the two isotopes have the same chemical properties. part b, State one physical property that is different for the two isotopes and explain why.
Chemistry depends on electrons, which are identical. Mass and density differ because bromine eighty one has two more neutrons, so a heavier nucleus for essentially the same size.
Answer part a, in terms of electrons and part b, in terms of neutrons.
For part b, name a physical property linked to mass, then trace it back to the nucleus.
In, b, link the difference in the nucleus to a quantity you could measure for a sample.
At the same temperature and pressure, thirty seven chlorine two gas is denser than thirty five chlorine two gas. What is the best explanation?

Each chlorine thirty seven atom has two more neutrons, so each molecule is heavier, while equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure hold the same number of molecules, mass divided by volume is therefore larger. The isotopes have the same proton number and the same electron configuration, the other three statements are false.
Density is mass divided by volume. Which of these does the extra particle change?
Isotopes have the same numbers of protons and electrons, so cross out anything that changes those.
For the options left, check that the statement about mass and about volume are both true for gases at the same temperature and pressure.
Explain why isotopes of the same element have different masses.
Isotopes have different numbers of neutrons, and neutrons contribute to the mass of the nucleus, so the atoms have different masses.
Which particle count differs between isotopes?
Protons and neutrons make up almost all the mass of an atom.
More neutrons give a heavier atom.
Which property is greater for thirty seven chlorine two than for thirty five chlorine two at the same temperature and pressure?
Each chlorine thirty seven atom has two more neutrons, so a mole of molecules has a larger mass and the gas is denser. Protons, electrons and ion formation are identical.
Which of these depends on mass, and which on protons and electrons?
The two gases differ only in the number of neutrons in the nuclei.
For each option, ask whether it would change if every nucleus gained two neutrons.

Equal volumes of thirty five chlorine two and thirty seven chlorine two are measured at the same temperature and pressure. Take the molar mass of each atom as equal to its nucleon number in g moles minus one. Calculate the ratio density of thirty seven chlorine two, all over, density of thirty five chlorine two.
Equal volumes at the same T and p contain equal numbers of moles, so the density ratio equals the ratio of molar masses, seventy four over seventy equals one point zero five seven.
Equal volumes of gas at the same T and p contain the same amount in moles.
So the density ratio is the ratio of the molar masses of the two molecules.
Molar mass of a diatomic molecule is twice that of an atom, put the heavier isotope on top.

Deuterium, hydrogen two, atomic number one, is an isotope of hydrogen, hydrogen one, atomic number one. part a, State the number of neutrons in one atom of deuterium. part b, Deuterium gas, D two, has a molar mass of four point zero zero grams per mole. Calculate its density at r. t. p. in grams per cubic decimetre. Take the molar volume at r. t. p. as twenty four point zero cubic decimetres per mole. part c, Explain why D two has the same chemical properties as H two but a different density.

Neutrons equals two minus one equals one. Density equals four point zero zero over twenty four point zero equals zero point one six seven grams per cubic decimetre. The isotopes have the same electrons, same chemistry, but different masses, different density.
Part part a, uses nucleon number and proton number, part part b, is density equals mass divided by volume for one mole.
In part b, use one mole of D two and the molar volume at r. t. p. twenty four point zero cubic decimetres per mole.
For part c, contrast electrons with neutrons, which set is the same, and which set changes mass?
A single phosphorus thirty two nucleus can be produced when a single sulfur thirty two nucleus joins with particle X. In the process a proton is emitted. What is particle X?
one point two Isotopes.
In one breath.

Isotopes are atoms of the same element that differ only in their number of neutrons. Because the electrons are identical the chemistry is identical, but the extra mass changes physical properties such as density.
Key ideas.

Isotopes are atoms of the same element, same number of protons, that is, the same proton number, with different numbers of neutrons, and so different nucleon numbers. Both halves of that sentence earn the marks.
Nuclide notation, in x y amperes, x is the nucleon, mass, number, protons plus neutrons, and y is the proton, atomic, number.
neutrons equals x minus y, electrons equals y minus q, for an ion of charge q plus.
A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons. The charge changes only the electrons, never the protons or neutrons.

Same chemical properties, chemical reactions involve the electrons, especially the outer ones. Isotopes have the same number of protons and so the same number of electrons and the same electron configuration. Neutrons have no charge and do not take part.

Different physical properties, isotopes have different numbers of neutrons, so their atoms have different masses. Properties that depend on mass, such as the density of a sample of the substance, differ.

Figure, Protium, deuterium and tritium, labelled protons, neutrons and electrons, source, nine seven zero one c1.2, p.3. Notice that each atom has one proton and one electron, while the neutron count and upper number in the isotope symbol increase together.
Method.
Read the symbol, top number x is the nucleon number, bottom number y is the proton number.
Protons equals y. Neutrons equals x minus y.
Electrons, start from y, then subtract q for a positive ion or add q for a negative ion.
Nuclear equations, balance the top numbers, then separately balance the bottom numbers, to find the missing particle.
Explanations, name the particle, electrons or neutrons, then say what it controls, chemistry or mass.
Worked example.
Particle X is formed in aluminium twenty seven, atomic number thirteen, plus helium four, atomic number two, gives phosphorus thirty, atomic number fifteen, plus X. Identify X.
Top numbers, twenty seven plus four equals thirty one and thirty one equals thirty plus x, so x equals one.
Nucleon numbers must balance on their own.
Bottom numbers, thirteen plus two equals fifteen and fifteen equals fifteen plus y, so y equals zero.
The proton numbers must balance separately.
Nucleon number one with no charge is a neutron, a neutron.
An electron has nucleon number zero and a proton has proton number one.
Traps.

Trap, atoms with the same mass number are isotopes. Why it's wrong, argon forty, forty kelvin and calcium forty have different proton numbers, so they are different elements. Instead, check the proton number first.
Trap, isotopes differ in protons or electrons. Why it's wrong, the proton number defines the element and a neutral atom has as many electrons as protons. Instead, only the neutrons change.
Trap, balancing only one of the two numbers in a nuclear equation. Why it's wrong, an electron or a proton can fix one row but breaks the other. Instead, balance both rows.
Trap, extra neutrons make an isotope react differently. Why it's wrong, chemistry depends on the electron configuration, which does not change. Instead, say same electrons, same chemical properties.
Trap, isotopes have identical physical properties. Why it's wrong, extra neutrons add mass. Instead, say different mass and different density.
Exam technique.
Define needs the full definition, same number of protons and different number of neutrons. Different mass number alone is too vague.

Explain needs a reason in terms of particles. Examiners see many candidates give a basic definition and then fail to link it to chemical and physical properties, so always finish the link, same electrons, so same chemistry, different neutrons, so different mass.
For density of a gas at r. t. p. use rho equals M over V m with V m equals twenty four point zero cubic decimetres per mole, and double the atomic molar mass for a diatomic gas.
Give proton, neutron and electron counts as whole numbers, and check the sign of the charge.
